findings.reason: a worker following the bullet rebuilds a cache that exists and leaves the repeated covered-tree walk in place, so the first done-when case ("list the directory once") still fails.
findings.text: s13 says resource identity resolution will "answer from one directory index per process, keyed on the directory's signature through `reckon/file_memo.py`", but `_directory_identity_index` already does exactly that (`reckon/resources.py:851-878`: `_INDEX_MEMO[key] = (listing, index)`, reused while `stored[0] == listing`, and the listing's entries are `file_memo.file_signature(path)` at `:831`); what actually costs the 19 % is `_identity_listing` calling `metadata_index._reuse_covered` on every resolve (`:816`), before the memo is consulted at `:859` — the validation-repeated defect §4's descope note says is fixed by entering `resources.resource_scan_scope`, which `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py` never enters (no `resource_scan_scope` or `discovery_file_scope` anywhere in it)

findings.reason: the section cannot be closed on the measure it declares unless the worktree cost is made mandatory, and no reader can tell from the shares whether the bar is reachable at all.
findings.text: the done-when requires the after wall time "at most half the before figure", while the profile the section rests on puts 29 % — its largest single cost — in `routing._create_worktree`, a cost the deliverable explicitly leaves optional ("why the worktree creation stays as it is or how it was shortened"); the three costs it does name total 48 %, so even a perfect implementation lands near the bar, and the 28 % "in `pathlib.stat` overall" is listed beside them as though the five shares were a partition of one budget

findings.reason: a third of the deliverable is unmeasurable as written, so a worker can pass every case without touching it, and a worker that reads it literally will change nothing.
findings.text: "the capability record is read once per dispatch" is in the deliverable but has no case in the done-when, no negative control and no count; `_recorded_capability` has exactly one call site (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2853`), so as written it names no repeat to remove and the 14 % is really the cost inside `resolve_section_routing` when the route carries no `section_routing` evidence (`:1350-1357`), a function the section never names

findings.reason: the read is the section's only evidence that anything improved, and as written it can pass or fail on machine noise or on which moment the worker chose to measure.
findings.text: the timer arm is "the same timer, run on the live store before and after … at a comparable load", which defines no load, no repeat count and no tolerance, on a section that itself records the store running at load average 80 to 120, and it carries no negative control of the kind §7 declares for its own timer; the "before" figure is also the one the Why says never completed — three calls ran past their 300 to 560 s bound without creating a review — so a before wall time may not exist to divide by

findings.reason: the dispatch contract already places logs under the run's own directory, so a worker's default lands durably even without the clause.
findings.text: s13 requires a live-store timer and a 60 s `py-spy --idle` profile but declares no containing path, while §7 ("the log, under the run's `logs/`"), §9 ("every log is under the run directory") and §10 ("every command is logged under the run directory") each declare one
